nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiMoO₄ synthesis
nodes.procedure: 581.2 mg of (NH₄)₆Mo₇O₂₄·4H₂O and 618 mg of Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O are dissolved in 30 mL of deionized water, stirred for 30 minutes, and the resulting mixed solution together with a pretreated piece of nickel foam (NF) is transferred into a 50 mL polytetrafluoroethylene-lined container, which is then positioned inside a stainless steel autoclave and reacted at 150°C for 6 h. Once the reaction vessel has reached room temperature, the obtained precursor is collected, washed with deionized water and ethanol to remove surface contaminants, and dried in a vacuum oven at 60°C for 12 h to yield NiMoO₄.

nodes.name: Ion exchange PBA formation
nodes.procedure: Dissolved 200 mg of K3[Fe(CN)6] thoroughly in 30 mL of deionized water, then fully immersed the NiMoO4 in this solution, and allowed the reaction to proceed at 60°C for 2 h. Subsequently, extracted the material, cleansed meticulously with deionized water and ethanol, desiccated, and thus acquired NiMoO4@PBA.

nodes.name: Phosphorization to P-NiMoO4@Fe2O3
nodes.procedure: During the phosphating process, 1.5 g of NaH2PO2 and NiMoO4@PBA were placed in two porcelain boats, positioning them at the inlet and outlet of a tubular furnace. Then, Ar gas was introduced with a flow rate set to 100 sccm. The temperature was raised from ambient conditions to 350°C at a rate of 2°C per minute and held at this temperature for 2 h. After cooling, P-NiMoO4@Fe2O3 was obtained.

Using a conventional three-electrode configuration in 1 M KOH solution, the HER properties were evaluated, applying an 85% iR correction. As illustrated in Fig. 3a, P-NiMoO4@Fe2O3 displayed excellent HER performance characterized by overpotentials of 45, 164, and 246 mV at 10, 100, and 300 mA cm⁻², respectively.

The OER property of P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃... was evaluated through various electrochemical tests in a 1 M KOH solution. Fig. 4a shows that the P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃ needed overpotentials of 210, 242, and 302 mV to deliver current densities of 10, 100, and 500 mA cm⁻², respectively.

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in alkaline electrolyzer
nodes.source_text: The water electrolysis device assembled with P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃||P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃ achieved a current density of 10 mA cm⁻² at an applied voltage of only 1.53 V... demonstrated a stable chronoamperometry curve at a high current density of 100 mA cm⁻²... indicating near 100% Faradaic efficiency (FE) for HER and OER.

nodes.characterization_summary: Perfectly arranged hollow nanorod arrays of P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃ grow densely and uniformly on NF surface with nanorod diameter around 300 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Perfectly arranged hollow nanorod arrays of P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃ grow densely and uniformly on the surface of NF (Fig. 1b, 1c, and Fig. S7).

properties.description: High-resolution image showing nanostructured material with porous, sheet-like morphology and square-like openings

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms inner layer P-NiMoO₄ and outer layer Fe₂O₃ in the nanorods of P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM image confirmed that the inner layer of the nanorods was P-NiMoO₄, while the outer layer was Fe₂O₃ (Fig. 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM shows lattice fringes of 0.34 nm (121) and 0.26 nm (104) for NiMoO₄ and Fe₂O₃ respectively with clear heterointerfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) image of P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃ showed lattice fringes of 0.34 and 0.26 nm, attributed to the (121) and (104) crystal planes of NiMoO₄ and Fe₂O₃, respectively (Fig. 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDS confirm Mo and Fe inside/outside nanorods with even distribution of Ni, O, P in P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃ heterojunction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM and corresponding energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) images verified the existence of Mo and Fe inside and outside the nanorods, respectively, and the even distribution of Ni, O, and P.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows NiMoO₄ diffraction peaks matching standard pattern, NiFe PBA peaks in NiMoO₄@PBA, and NiMoO₄ + Fe₂O₃ (104 at 33.2°) peaks in P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Diffraction peaks corresponding to NiMoO₄ and Fe₂O₃ (PDF# No.89-8103) were observed in the XRD pattern of P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃. The peaks at 33.2° of the crystal faces of Fe₂O₃ (104) were clearly identified.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Mo-O (~356 cm⁻¹), Mo-O-Ni (~800-1000 cm⁻¹) in all samples; Fe-CN-Ni (~2187 cm⁻¹) in NiMoO₄@PBA; Fe-O (~650-720 cm⁻¹) in P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Mo-O (~356 cm⁻¹) and Mo-O-Ni (~800-1000 cm⁻¹) related vibration peaks were observed in NiMoO₄, NiMoO₄@PBA and P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃... Fe-O (~650-720 cm⁻¹) peak appeared in the P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey confirms presence of Ni, Mo, Fe, O, P in P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃. Ni 2p peaks at 874.1/856.2 eV (Ni²⁺) shift negatively by 0.46/0.88 eV vs NiMoO₄/P-NiMoO₄. Mo 3d shows Mo⁴⁺ (234.1/230.3 eV) and Mo⁶⁺ (235.4/232.2 eV). Fe 2p shows Fe³⁺ (725.9/713.4 eV), Fe²⁺ (724.1/711.0 eV), Fe⁰ (719.9/707.1 eV). P 2p shows P-O (134.1 eV), P-metal (129.9 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The full spectrum in Fig. 2c confirmed the presence of Ni, Mo, Fe, O and P elements in the P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃. The Ni 2p spectra of P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃ exhibited peaks at 874.1 and 856.2 eV... Compared with NiMoO₄ and P-NiMoO₄, the binding energy of Ni 2p in P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃ shifted negatively by 0.46/0.88 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows stronger signal at g=2.003 for P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃ than NiMoO₄, indicating more oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃ showed a stronger signal at g = 2.003 than that of the NiMoO₄, implying that there were more defects in P-NiMoO₄@Fe₂O₃.
